hebrewText: יְנַקֵּ֣שׁ נ֭וֹשֶׁה לְ/כָל אֲשֶׁר ל֑/וֹ וְ/יָבֹ֖זּוּ זָרִ֣ים יְגִיעֽ/וֹ

tokens.bdb: to entrap (with a noose), literally or figuratively
to lend or (by reciprocity) borrow on security or interest
tokens.kjv: creditor, exact, extortioner, lend, usurer, lend on (taker on) usury.
tokens.ptLiteralWord: to lend or  borrow on security or interest
tokens.enLiteralWord: to lend or  borrow on security or interest
tokens.explanation: to lend or  borrow on security or interest
tokens.explanationEn: to lend or  borrow on security or interest

tokens.bdb: properly, the whole; hence, all, any or every (in the singular only, but often in a plural sense)
tokens.kjv: (in) all (manner, (ye)), altogether, any (manner), enough, every (one, place, thing), howsoever, as many as, (no-) thing, ought, whatsoever, (the) whole, whoso(-ever).

tokens.bdb: who, which, what, that; also (as an adverb and a conjunction) when, where, how, because, in order that, etc.
tokens.kjv: [idiom] after, [idiom] alike, as (soon as), because, [idiom] every, for, [phrase] forasmuch, [phrase] from whence, [phrase] how(-soever), [idiom] if, (so) that ((thing) which, wherein), [idiom] though, [phrase] until, [phrase] whatsoever, when, where ([phrase] -as, -in, -of, -on, -soever, -with), which, whilst, [phrase] whither(-soever), who(-m, -soever, -se). As it is indeclinable, it is often accompanied by the personal pronoun expletively, used to show the connection.
catch, gather, (take) for a prey, rob(-ber), spoil, take (away, spoil), [idiom] utterly.

tokens.bdb: to turn aside (especially for lodging); hence to be aforeigner, strange, profane; specifically (active participle) to commit adultery
tokens.kjv: (come from) another (man, place), fanner, go away, (e-) strange(-r, thing, woman).
tokens.ptLiteralWord: to turn aside ; hence to be aforeigner
tokens.enLiteralWord: to turn aside ; hence to be aforeigner
tokens.explanation: to turn aside ; hence to be aforeigner
tokens.explanationEn: to turn aside ; hence to be aforeigner

tokens.bdb: toil; hence, a work, produce, property (as the result of labor)
